newsletter.markdown:
1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

* **[Biotech]** **[Arrowhead reports preclinical and early clinical validation of CNS RNAi delivery](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/arrowhead-rnai-alzheimers-tau-aro-mapt-study-results/832950/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Arrowhead's experimental RNAi drug ARO-MAPT lowered tau protein levels by an average of 73% at its highest dose after 105 days in an early trial involving healthy volunteers (administered via two injections spaced two weeks apart).
  - The findings provide clinical validation for a delivery platform enabling RNA-modulating treatments to cross the blood-brain barrier and target the central nervous system, suggesting a dosing regimen of once every three months.

* **[Biotech]** **[Analysis highlights high attrition rates against canonically undruggable targets](https://x.com/andrewpannu/status/2110377535565434965)** — *X / Twitter*
  - An evaluation of ~160 undruggable cancer targets and 17 active targets (~80 total programs) reveals that ~40% of clinical programs have stalled, and ~75% of small molecule programs against these targets are discontinued.
  - Unlike the KRAS paradigm, active clinical programs increasingly avoid hidden binding sites in favor of modalities like RNA, engineered T-cells, or degraders, with large pharma favoring peripheral platform-oriented business development over direct asset licensing.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

* **[Biotech]** **[Verastem shares rise on Phase 1/2 KRAS G12D cancer data](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/verastem-g12d-pancreatic-cancer-results-genfleet/832952/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - Verastem Oncology released early data for VS-7375, an experimental small molecule designed to bind to both the "on" and "off" states of KRAS G12D mutations across metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, metastatic colorectal cancer, and advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
  - Based on these Phase 1/2 results, the company plans to initiate three late-stage trials before the end of June.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Johnson & Johnson reports Phase 2 icotrokinra data in ulcerative colitis](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2604435?af=R&rss=currentIssue)** — *New England Journal of Medicine*
  - Results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating oral icotrokinra in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis were published, detailing efficacy and safety outcomes in this mid-stage population.

* **[Biotech]** **[Antengene enters clinical collaboration with Eli Lilly and Merck KGaA](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2110688291578106124)** — *X / Twitter*
  - Antengene partnered to evaluate the combination of AN4035 and cetuximab.
  - Cetuximab will be supplied by Eli Lilly for US trial sites and by Merck KGaA for Australia and China trial sites.

* **[Biotech]** **[Cellectar Biosciences reports subset data for iopofosine I 131](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2110687781987217419)** — *X / Twitter*
  - Presented subset analysis data from the Phase 2b CLOVER WaM trial evaluating iopofosine I 131 in patients with Waldenström's macroglobulinemia relapsed or refractory to BTK inhibitor therapy.

3. **Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III**

* **[Ponatinib–blinatumomab outpaces imatinib–chemotherapy in Ph-positive ALL](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2606208?af=R&rss=currentIssue)** — *New England Journal of Medicine*
  - A pivotal comparative study demonstrated superior efficacy for the chemotherapy-free regimen of ponatinib combined with blinatumomab compared with imatinib combined with chemotherapy in adult patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

* **[Continuous glucose monitoring evaluated in non–insulin-treated type 2 diabetes](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2608571?af=R&rss=currentIssue)** — *New England Journal of Medicine*
  - Published ahead of print evaluating clinical utility and outcomes of continuous glucose monitoring devices in patients managing type 2 diabetes without insulin therapy.

* **[Renal-replacement therapy modality comparisons in acute kidney injury](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2608397?af=R&rss=currentIssue)** — *New England Journal of Medicine*
  - Ahead-of-print trial data comparing intermittent versus continuous renal-replacement therapy approaches in critically ill patients presenting with acute kidney injury.

4. **Regulatory & Approvals**

* **[Biotech]** **[FDA expands indication for Anktiva in bladder cancer](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-treatment-certain-people-bcg-unresponsive-bladder-cancer)** — *FDA News Release*
  - Expanded the approval of Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) plus Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) to include adults with BCG-unresponsive high-grade papillary-only non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
  - Backed by evidence from cohort data of the single-arm QUILT-3.032 trial (NCT03022825), marking a shifting regulatory approach to evaluating evidence across related bladder cancer forms.

* **[Biotech]** **[Aquestive Therapeutics secures FDA NDA resubmission acceptance for Anaphylm](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2110687491766267972)** — *X / Twitter*
  - The FDA accepted the resubmitted New Drug Application, setting a PDUFA action date of March 16, 2027.

* **[FDA launches Rare Disease Framework Initiative](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-rare-disease-framework-initiative-develop-holistic-fit-purpose-framework-rare-disease)** — *FDA News Release*
  - Announced a new initiative alongside a white paper to build an optimized, fit-for-purpose drug development and review framework tailored to small patient populations and realistic evidence generation.
  - A hybrid public meeting in partnership with the Reagan-Udall Foundation is scheduled for October 28, 2026, at the FDA White Oak campus.

* **[Trump administration delays foreign prescription drug import rule](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/14/trump-administration-delays-new-rule-that-could-restrict-imported-meds-from-canad-and-overseas/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  - The federal government pushed back by 90 days the implementation of a new rule that could potentially restrict Americans from sourcing prescription medications from licensed international pharmacies, including those in Canada.

5. **Business & Strategy**

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Gilead Sciences and Vir Biotechnology form T-cell engager collaboration](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/jnj-earnings-gilead-vir-shkreli-pfizer/832879/)** — *BioPharma Dive / [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2110349122733498416)*
  - Gilead Sciences entered into a multi-program collaboration and license agreement with Vir Biotechnology to discover and develop novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager therapies for solid tumors.
  - Vir will receive a USD 90 million upfront payment, comprising USD 65 million in cash and a USD 25 million equity investment at a 30% premium.

* **[Biotech]** **[Iambic Therapeutics completes $150M IPO](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/iambic-ipo-price-ai-drug-discovery/832771/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - AI-driven drug discovery startup Iambic raised $150 million through the pricing of 9.4 million shares at $16 each on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol IAM.
  - The company has secured $462 million in private funding since 2019 to advance its pipeline, anchored by its lead targeted cancer therapy entering early human clinical testing.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Sanofi settles EU antitrust probe over rival vaccine disparagement](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/14/sanofi-avoids-fine-as-eu-accepts-offer-ends-antitrust-probe-over-disparaging-rival-vaccine/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  - European Union antitrust regulators accepted structural concessions from Sanofi to close an investigation into an allegedly misleading marketing campaign targeting a competing influenza vaccine, allowing the company to avoid financial penalties.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[CVS Health agrees to $315M opioid settlement](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/cvs-pay-315-million-settle-opioid-prescribing-allegations/832999/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  - CVS Pharmacy agreed to pay $315 million to resolve Department of Justice allegations regarding the dispensing of medically unnecessary opioid prescriptions and associated Medicare reimbursement violations, without admitting wrongdoing.

* **[Biotech]** **[Ultragenyx sells rare disease priority review voucher](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2110348334015676625)** — *X / Twitter*
  - Sold its rare pediatric disease priority review voucher for USD 203 million.

* **[Armed Cell Therapeutics acquires former Galapagos CAR-T assets](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2110635727004340599)** — *X / Twitter*
  - Paul Stoffels has taken over as CEO of Armed Cell Therapeutics, which acquired former Galapagos CAR-T assets for 8 million Euros.

6. **Public Health & Policy**

* **[Former FDA leadership criticizes DOGE workforce reductions](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/14/former-fda-commissioners-say-recruit-defend-support-agency-workforce/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  - Three former FDA commissioners publicly condemned government efficiency (DOGE) budget cuts, warning that the departures have stripped the agency of institutional expertise that will take years to rebuild.

* **[CDC survey highlights adolescent binge eating rates](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/15/teenage-binge-eating-cdc-survey-finds-alarming-rate/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT*
  - A new Centers for Disease Control and Prevention survey reports that approximately 40% of high school students experienced binge eating during the preceding month.

**Worth watching:** Arrowhead's clinical CNS delivery validation for RNAi, which could unlock previously undruggable neurodegenerative targets alongside the FDA's newly launched Rare Disease Framework.
